parole.testo: Borrowed from Língua Geral Paulista *ka'aatãtuva, from ka'a (“vegetation”) + atã (“hard”) + tuva (“gathering”). First attested in 1769.

parole.significato: bamboo of the species Eremocaulon asymmetricum
parole.testo: Borrowed from Língua Geral Paulista. First attested in 1863.

parole.significato: Nickname given in Colonial Brazil by bandeirantes and their descendants to Portuguese and other outsiders lured by gold…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Língua Geral Paulista mboaba.

parole.significato: any tree in the genus Aspidosperma
parole.testo: According to Navarro, from Língua Geral Paulista, but he gives no further etymology.

Uncertain. Navarro hypothesizes a shortening of Língua Geral Paulista kulumĩ (“boy”). Other sources point to the same origin of etymology 1, saying the Old Tupi term only referred to young catfish. Compare Spanish gurí.
